title: Silicon Valley S06E01

completeness.note: All required fields are present and non-empty, including genre, pacing, mood, tags, topics, audience, visual style, and hook. Several entries are thin theme labels rather than sharp descriptors.

specificity.note: Tags stay at series-level abstractions (data privacy, ethics, power dynamics) and never name episode-specific beats such as the congressional testimony, Colin’s data grab, the Gilfoyle/Dinesh AIs, Gwart, or Hooli.

fidelity.note: The data-ethics clash is in the right neighborhood, but Silicon Valley is a comedy mislabeled as drama, with a tense/reflective tone. Decentralization, surveillance, personal betrayals, and the orange-blue palette are not supported by the synopsis.

consistency.note: Genre, mood, ethics tags, and the ethical-crisis hook form a coherent serious-drama package. Decentralization sits loosely beside the privacy-and-greed story but does not contradict it.

recsys_usefulness.note: Privacy and tech-industry tags could retrieve some adjacent viewers, but a drama label and missing satire would steer the episode away from comedy audiences and toward the wrong tone.

summary: The metadata is complete and internally coherent as a tech-ethics drama, but it misses that this is a comedy and replaces the episode’s concrete plots with generic or unsupported claims. It would not reliably recommend Silicon Valley S06E01 to the right viewers.
